spike: SPIKE 1 — InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair() as the test seam, and McpServer vs Server for verbatim JSON Schema passthrough (OpenAPI bridge)
claim: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` exports `InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair()`, and a linked pair carries a real MCP session (initialize + tools/list + tools/call) between an in-process server and a real `Client`, with no child process and no port. Sub-claims: the import specifier is `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/inMemory.js`; the low-level `Server` + `setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, …)` accepts a plain JSON Schema `inputSchema` untouched while the high-level `McpServer.registerTool` demands Zod; the pair survives `close()` on one side.
verdict: CONFIRMED (main claim fully; the McpServer-vs-Server sub-question resolved AGAINST the high-level API — use low-level `Server` for the catalog)

evidence:
All paths under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-nguyenhanh-orca-projects-MCPRouter/4911361f-32f3-47c8-97c7-182f1fc87bd2/scratchpad/spikes/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/`:

- `package.json` exports map has a `"./*"` wildcard → `./dist/esm/*`, which is what resolves `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/inMemory.js`. There is no dedicated `"./inMemory"` export key.
- `dist/esm/inMemory.d.ts:19` — `static createLinkedPair(): [InMemoryTransport, InMemoryTransport];`
- `dist/esm/inMemory.js:11-17` — createLinkedPair sets `_otherTransport` on both sides.
- `dist/esm/inMemory.js:25-30` — `close()` nulls `_otherTransport`, awaits `other?.close()`, then fires `onclose` → closing one side closes both.
- `dist/esm/inMemory.js:36-38` — `send()` throws `new Error('Not connected')` once `_otherTransport` is gone.
- `dist/esm/inMemory.js:35-44` — `send(message, options)` forwards `{ authInfo: options?.authInfo }` as the handler `extra`; queues if the peer has no `onmessage` yet (so connect order does not matter).
- `dist/esm/server/zod-compat.d.ts:3` — `export type AnySchema = z3.ZodTypeAny | z4.$ZodType;` — "AnySchema" in `registerTool` means Zod only, never JSON Schema.
- `dist/esm/server/mcp.d.ts:150-157` — `registerTool<OutputArgs extends ZodRawShapeCompat | AnySchema, InputArgs extends undefined | ZodRawShapeCompat | AnySchema>`.
- `dist/esm/server/mcp.js:865-870` — `getZodSchemaObject()`: `if (!isZodSchemaInstance(schema)) throw new Error('inputSchema must be a Zod schema or raw shape, received an unrecognized object')`. Called from `_createRegisteredTool` at `mcp.js:611`, i.e. at REGISTRATION time.
- `dist/esm/server/mcp.js:67-98` — McpServer's own `ListToolsRequestSchema` handler regenerates the JSON Schema with `toJsonSchemaCompat(obj, {strictUnions:true, pipeStrategy:'input'})`. There is no verbatim path through McpServer.
- `dist/esm/types.js:1229-1249` — `ToolSchema.inputSchema = z.object({type: z.literal('object'), properties: z.record(z.string(), AssertObjectSchema).optional(), required: z.array(z.string()).optional()}).catchall(z.unknown())` — the `catchall` is why `$defs`/`title`/`additionalProperties`/`x-*` survive.
- `dist/esm/types.js:13` — `const AssertObjectSchema = z.custom(v => v !== null && (typeof v === 'object' || typeof v === 'function'))` — `z.custom` returns the value untouched, so every nested property schema (`$ref`, `oneOf`, `format`, `enum`) passes through unmodified.
impact:
Two changes to spec §14 / the catalog design.

1. The test seam is confirmed as designed — `InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair()` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/inMemory.js` carries a full initialize + tools/list + tools/call session in-process. No fallback needed, the ~50 LOC hand-written transport pair is dead budget, delete it from the plan.

2. The catalog MUST use the low-level `Server` + `setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, …)`, not `McpServer.registerTool`. `McpServer` throws at REGISTRATION time on a plain JSON Schema (`inputSchema must be a Zod schema or raw shape, received an unrecognized object`), and even when fed Zod it re-derives the JSON Schema through `toJsonSchemaCompat` — draft-07 `$schema`, an injected `maximum: 9007199254740991` on ints, a 200-char regex `pattern` bolted onto `format: date-time`. Nothing survives verbatim through the high-level API. If the design currently says "McpServer" anywhere in that ~110 LOC, flip it to `Server`; the verbatim-passthrough property the OpenAPI bridge depends on is a property of the low-level API only. The upside: `Server` does ZERO validation of `tools/call` arguments, so the gateway forwards the raw object as intended (validation is the upstream's job) — no Zod-shape conversion layer anywhere in the catalog.
fallback_verified: Not needed and not run — the claim held, so the hand-written linked-transport fallback is unnecessary. The one sub-claim that failed (high-level `McpServer` + JSON Schema) has its fallback already inside the SDK: the low-level `Server`, which I did run end to end in spike-1-inmemory.mjs section 1 and it passed `assert.deepStrictEqual` on the round-tripped schema.
gotchas: `new Server(info, {capabilities: {tools: {}}})` — the capabilities argument is not optional in practice. Omit it and `setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, …)` throws `assertCanSetRequestHandler`. McpServer registers it for you; Server does not.

Verbatim means CONTENT, not BYTES. Zod's object parse reorders keys: declared keys (`type`, `properties`, `required`) are emitted first, then `catchall` keys. Sent `type,x-vendor,properties,zzz,required` → received `type,properties,required,x-vendor,zzz`. `assert.deepStrictEqual` passes, `JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b)` FAILS. Anything hashing a serialized schema for a catalog etag or cache key must canonicalize first, or every upstream refresh will look like a change.

`ToolSchema.inputSchema` requires `type: 'object'` at the ROOT, enforced client-side as `z.literal('object')`. A tool with `inputSchema: {type:'string'}` or with `inputSchema` omitted entirely makes the CLIENT's `listTools()` reject the whole response with a `$ZodError` — one bad tool poisons the entire catalog page, not just that entry. The OpenAPI bridge must wrap any non-object operation body in an object envelope, and the aggregator should validate each upstream tool before merging it into a page.

The low-level `Server` performs NO validation of `tools/call` arguments against the advertised `inputSchema` — the handler received `{status:'open',page:3}` exactly as sent. Good for a gateway (pure passthrough), but it means MCPRouter is not a validating boundary; do not let the spec claim it is.

`close()` on ONE transport closes BOTH: `InMemoryTransport.close()` awaits `other?.close()` before firing its own `onclose`. Both `server.onclose` and `client.onclose` fired from a single `clientTransport.close()`. Subsequent requests reject with a plain `Error: Not connected` (not an `McpError`), so error-mapping code must handle that string. Calling `close()` repeatedly on both sides is safe — no throw.

Connect order does not matter: `send()` queues into the peer's `_messageQueue` when the peer has no `onmessage` yet, and `start()` drains it. `Promise.all([server.connect(st), client.connect(ct)])` works, and so does connecting either side first.

`InMemoryTransport.send(msg, {authInfo})` injects an `AuthInfo` that arrives as `extra.authInfo` in the low-level request handler — verified with `{token:'tok',clientId:'cid',scopes:['a']}`. That is the seam for testing MCPRouter's per-request auth without standing up better-auth or an HTTP server.

The import specifier resolves through the package's `"./*"` wildcard export, so the `.js` extension is mandatory: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/inMemory.js` works, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/inMemory` does not.
